headline: Dry with lifting fog this afternoon and more fog Saturday morning, then light rain Saturday afternoon and evening, followed by a much stormier stretch next week with repeated rounds of rain, mountain snow, strong winds and a growing coastal-flood threat.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Friday began cold and foggy across the Puget Sound lowlands, with morning lows in the low to mid 30s (upper 20s in a few spots south of the Sound) and freezing fog in colder parts of the southwest interior. High pressure keeps the day dry, and the fog is slowly lifting and breaking up, with clearer skies expected by early afternoon; highs reach the mid to upper 40s inland and the low 50s on the coast. Fog and freezing fog are expected to form again tonight into Saturday morning, though incoming high clouds may keep the thickest fog mostly in the south interior around Olympia, with lows in the upper 20s to mid 30s.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: On Saturday a low-pressure system drops south from the northeast Pacific and parks offshore through Sunday, bringing rain to the coast by late Saturday morning and to the interior, including Puget Sound and the north Olympic Peninsula, by late afternoon. Amounts stay light through Sunday: only a few hundredths of an inch in the interior lowlands and around a tenth of an inch on the Central Coast. Snow levels hover near 2,000 feet, so the Cascade passes could pick up a light coating of snow (under an inch). Highs both days run in the mid 40s to low 50s.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: On Monday the offshore low is swept away as a larger low-pressure system drops in from the Aleutians and strengthens off the coast Monday night into Tuesday. That sets up an active pattern through Thursday, with several disturbances bringing multiple rounds of widespread lowland rain, mountain snow and gusty winds, including strong winds along the Strait of Juan de Fuca on Tuesday. Rivers will start to rise; no widespread river flooding is expected, but the Skokomish River will likely reach flood stage mid to late week.

coast: Calm on the water today, though fog may cover the inland waters, with a 50–60% chance of visibility under 1 nautical mile on the Central and South Sound this morning. Winds and seas pick up tonight: a Small Craft Advisory runs from 10 PM tonight into Saturday for the coastal waters and from 2 AM to 4 PM Saturday for the western Strait of Juan de Fuca, and a Gale Watch is up for the outer coastal waters Saturday morning and afternoon (50–70% chance of gales), with seas building to 10–13 feet by Sunday. A stronger system Monday into Tuesday is the bigger concern: gales are more than 70% likely on the coastal waters from late Monday morning, peaking early Tuesday with a 90%+ chance of gales and a 45–70% chance of storm-force winds offshore, plus a 50–70% chance of gales through the Strait of Juan de Fuca Tuesday and a 35–40% chance of an isolated storm-force gust in the Central and East Strait (the Port Angeles–Sequim stretch). Seas build toward 20 feet on the outer coast (25–35% chance of topping 20 feet), and small-craft-strength winds are 70–100% likely to continue on the coast and Strait midweek into late week, with seas likely staying above 10 feet. High astronomical tides may bring minor coastal flooding to the Pacific Coast and Strait of Juan de Fuca by Sunday, and the coastal-flood threat grows Tuesday into Wednesday, especially on the Pacific Coast as large waves build.
watch_for: Freezing fog again Saturday morning in colder spots, mainly the south and southwest interior.
Tuesday's storm: possible gales and isolated storm-force gusts through the Strait of Juan de Fuca near Port Angeles and Sequim.
Coastal flooding with high tides from Sunday into midweek, and the Skokomish River likely reaching flood stage mid to late week.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in today's dry, foggy weather and the light weekend rain, and highly confident in a stormy Monday–Tuesday on the water (90%+ odds of coastal gales), while how strong the peak winds get and exact rain totals next week remain less certain.
